```python
def extend_longest_diagonal_lines(grid, bg=None):
    """Extend to the grid edge only the longest non-background diagonal line(s) (ties all), through background."""
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]; h=len(g); w=len(g[0])
    bg=background(g) if bg is None else bg
    lines={}  # (dr,dc,diagonal_id) -> list of (r,c)
    for dr,dc in ((1,1),(1,-1)):
        for r in range(h):
            for c in range(w):
                if g[r][c]!=bg:
                    # diag id
                    k=dr, (r-c if dc==1 else r+c)
                    lines.setdefault(k,[]).append((r,c))
    if not lines: return g
    mx=max(len(v) for v in lines.values())
    for k,cells in lines.items():
        if len(cells)<2 or len(cells)<mx: continue
        v=g[cells[0][0]][cells[0][1]]  # hmm color of extension
        dr,dc=(1,1) if k[0]==1 else (1,-1)
        # actually need per-line direction: two diagonals share k? (1,1) uses r-c, (1,-1) uses r+c → distinct keys.
        for r,c in cells:
            for sgn in (1,-1):
                rr,cc=r+sgn*dr,c+sgn*dc
                while 0<=rr<h and 0<=cc<w and g[rr][cc]==bg:
                    g[rr][cc]=v; rr+=sgn*dr; cc+=sgn*dc
    return g
```
